messages.subject: Problem with the heigth scale
messages.body_plain:
Hey,
I'm doing microssatellite analysis to understand genetic relationship between fungal isolates. For that I first calculated the Jaccard’s coefficient and then want to generate a dendrogram using UPGMA cluster analysis.

I did the following:
## Distance matrix computation
jacc_coef <- vegdist(HC_df, method = "jaccard") *100
(HC_df is my data frame)
##Hierarchical clustering
afu_clin.hc <- hclust(d = jacc_coef, method = "average")

When I plot afu_clin.hc with another package I obtain the heigth scale corresponding to the % of dissimilarity that was calculated before.
HC = fviz_dend(x = afu_clin.hc, cex = 0.7, lwd = 0.7, horiz = TRUE)
print(HC)
I obtain the following plot:

However, when I try to use the ggtree the scale is different. I'm wondering how can I use ggtree to display my dendrogram with the height scale as % dissimilarity calculated with Jaccard’s coefficient.
I used this code:
hc_tree = ggtree(afu_clin.hc, size =0.8) + geom_tiplab(angle = 90, hjust=1, offset=-.05) + layout_dendrogram() + theme_dendrogram()

obtained this plot (I don't understand this scale, where does it come from?)

How can I use ggtree to plot a similar dendrogram to the one that I showed first?
Thank you,

Best
Daryna

messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I am having some trouble extrapolating this this tutorial <https://guangchuangyu.github.io/treedata-workshop/r-ggtree-data.html> and the %<+% operator.

What I want to do is close to the tutorial, I want to take a tree object and use a data-frame where one column is node-names and the second column holds numerical information per node. I want to attach the information from the data-frame to the tree object.

The data-frame looks something like this:

Node name > Count
A > 12
B > 14

So, I want to ultimately display the number 12 next to node A and number 14 next to node B while keeping the names intact. Now I have the code working up to the following point:
library(ggplot2)
library(ggtree)

x <- read.tree("raw_data/tree.txt")
info <- read.csv("raw_data/counts.csv",sep = '\t',header=TRUE)

p <- ggtree(x) %<+% info + xlim(-.1, 5)

p2 <- p + geom_tiplab(offset = 0.2) + geom_tippoint(aes(caption = Increase)) + theme_tree2()+geom_tiplab(align=TRUE, linesize=.5)+ xlim(0,25)

ggsave("test_2.pdf", width = 60, height = 80, units = "cm", limitsize = FALSE)

print(p2)

?geom_tippoint::aes() # is there a way to list all the option inside geom_tippoint::aes()

The above code overlays the Newick_label column with the node names instead of attaching the value in the second column.

But specifically, I am at a loss as to how I can list the options available within geom_tippoint(aes()). I can use ?geom_tippoint to access the documentation of geom_tippoint but I think my task needs to manipulate options within the aes() function and the the geom_tippoint() documentation does not list all the aes() options available. And am stuck trying different keywords for geom_tippoint(aes()).

Can my task be done in ggtree?

The tree and the count file are here <https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1VZhE3tOnpuzivVc06ZbSjEsoGHGbgib0?usp=sharing> if you want to give this a shot.

Sincerely,
Rijan

messages.subject: Annotating specific nodes
messages.body_plain:
I need to do something that seems like it should be simple in ggtree but I haven't been able to figure it out, and none of the examples in the documentation seem to be quite what I need.

I have a quite large tree (~5000 samples). In the paper I am going to show the full tree to show high-level patterns, and then a few figures that zoom in on very small clades. In the big full tree, I want to add labels on ONLY the ancestral nodes of the clades that I'm going to highlight later, to show where they are in the tree. So I want some kind of annotation where I can specify geom_something(node=1234, label="A") + geom_something(node=4321, label="B") or something along those lines. All of the documentation I can see for annotating nodes seems to require you to label every node. I don't want to use geom_cladelabel or geom_hilight because the clades are so small relative to the whole tree that they're not really visible when highlighted that way. I just want to be able to reference particular nodes in the tree. Any help would be appreciated!

messages.subject_clean: How to automatedly combine the bootstrap values from differet methods?
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone, when I do phylogenetic work, I often reconstruct the BI and ML trees at the same times based on the same data. And then I visualized them with combined the bootstrap maunally on Adobe Illustrator. So the modification is painful.

Now I want to change the visualization to ggtree and related packages. So any mehods can automated combine the bootstrap from different trees whose tip labels are same but topology may be not uniform?

ps: merge_tree seem to require the topology is uniform.

Any advises are welcome.

messages.subject: Re: How to automatedly combine the bootstrap values from differet methods?
messages.subject_clean: How to automatedly combine the bootstrap values from differet methods?
messages.body_plain:
Hi there.
I recommend transforming these trees into a tibble first (using the as_tibble() method) for a clearer view, then you can extract and merge the external data (i.e. bootstrap value) using tidyverse verbs, and eventually attach the merged data to the tree you want to visualize.
You can take a look at chapter 2 of the treedata book (http://yulab-smu.top/treedata-book/index.html). it should be helpful.
Hope this helps ;)

messages.subject_clean: How to automatedly combine the bootstrap values from differet methods?
messages.body_plain:
Thank william very much.
Based on your advise, I writed a script to finish the conbination of support values.
welcome to discuss for any possible bugs.

library(treedataverse)
setwd("c:/Users/qbycs/Desktop/ggteee/")
# 读取发育树
bitree <- read.mrbayes("bi.tre")
mltree <- read.tree("ml.tre")
# 转为tibble格式
bitree <- as_tibble(bitree)
mltree <- as_tibble(as.treedata(mltree))
#获取节点下所有样品的label
tiplabel <- function(x,y){
  tipnumber <- min(x$parent) - 1 # 获取tip label数量，即样品个数
  offspring(x,y)[which(offspring(x,y)$node <= tipnumber),]$label
}
for(i in sort(unique(bitree$parent))){
  # 获取该节点下的所有tip label
  tiplabel_under_node <- tiplabel(bitree,i)
# 寻找该节点在另一个发育树的对应节点
  somenode_in_other_tree <- MRCA(mltree, match(tiplabel_under_node,mltree$label))$node
# 判断两个节点下的tip label是否完全一样
  if(setequal(tiplabel(mltree,somenode_in_other_tree),tiplabel(bitree,i))){
    bitree[i,]$label <- paste(bitree[i,]$label,mltree[somenode_in_other_tree,]$label,sep = "/")
  } else {
    bitree[i,]$label <- paste(bitree[i,]$label,"-/-",sep = "/")
  }
}
write.tree(as.phylo(bitree),"combine-support.tre")
